title: HF469 (2017-2018 Regular): Minnesota Personal Protection Act amended, lifetime permits to carry handguns created, and application fee for permits to carry reduced.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2017/0/HF/469/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version (no date on file; 2017 session). The bill strikes the five-year expiry and the renewal process, including the renewal fee and late fee. Section 4 adjusts the records-purge rule (struck words 'or currently eligible to renew their permit').

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 2a): (a) An applicant must present evidence that the applicant received training in the safe use of a pistol within one year of the date of an application.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 3): (f) The sheriff may charge an application processing fee in an amount not to exceed the actual and reasonable direct cost of processing the application or $50, whichever is less.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 7): (c) A permit to carry a pistol issued under this section does not expire and permit cards issued after August 1, 2017, must prominently state that the permit does not expire.
Section 5 (replacement permits to carry): A person with a valid permit to carry a handgun issued under Minnesota Statutes, section 624.714, prior to August 1, 2017, shall request a replacement permit card that conforms with the requirements of Minnesota Statutes, section 624.714, subdivision 7, paragraph (c), prior to the expiration date listed on the permit holder's card.
